title: Bhakti Movement Groups Nirgun
definition: The Nirgun Bhakti tradition refers to the worship of a formless, abstract, and omnipresent God (Nirguna Brahman), rejecting idol worship, rituals, and the caste-based hierarchy of the Brahmanical order.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in Prelims (Art & Culture/History) regarding philosophy, key saints, and their literary contributions; Mains requires analysis of their role in social reform and egalitarianism.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Bhakti Movement Groups Nirgun.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Medieval Indian History
Understanding of Saguna vs Nirguna dichotomy
